extraFacts.fact: ISO 228-1 specifies pipe threads, designated G, where pressure-tight joints are not made on the threads: both the external and internal thread are parallel (BSPP). The seal is made by a washer, O-ring, bonded seal or sealing face, not by the thread flanks.
ISO 7-1 specifies pipe threads where pressure-tight joints are made on the threads: the external thread is a taper thread (designated R, BSPT) and the internal thread is parallel (Rp) or taper (Rc).

316L is the low-carbon grade of 316 austenitic stainless steel (carbon 0.03 % maximum), which is why it can be welded without carbide precipitation at the grain boundaries; it contains molybdenum for resistance to chloride pitting.
extraFacts.source: ASTM A240 / A276 chemical composition limits for UNS S31603

faqs.q: How do I tell whether a BSP Male Flat Seat or a 60° cone male is needed?

The two do not seal against each other, so check the seat before ordering, and see the [BSP male-parallel 60° cone](/p/bsp-male-parallel-60-cone) for the cone version.

faqs.q: What is the BSP Male Flat Seat made from, and where does stainless suit it?
faqs.a: The BSP Male Flat Seat is machined from 316L stainless steel, passivated with no plating, so its corrosion resistance comes from the native oxide layer. It suits marine, chemical, food-grade and washdown service where zinc-plated carbon steel corrodes. The listing gives -40°C to +200°C, limited by the hose and any O-ring.

faqs.q: Which standards does the BSP Male Flat Seat follow?

faqs.q: How is a BSP flat-seat male fitting tightened without leaking?

Lightly lubricate the stainless thread to prevent galling, and keep lubricant off the seat.

faqs.q: Where is the BSP swivel female flat seat (90° elbow) used in stainless hose assemblies?
faqs.a: It is used on stainless hose assemblies for BSPP equipment in marine, chemical and washdown service, where a hard right-angle turn is needed at the port. The [316L stainless hydraulic fittings guide](/blog/ss316l-hydraulic-fittings) covers the 316L material.

faqs.q: BSP swivel female flat seat (90° elbow) or BSP swivel female flat seat (45° elbow): which one do I order?
faqs.a: The 90° flat-seat elbow turns the hose through a right angle. The [BSP swivel female flat seat (45° elbow)](/p/bsp-swivel-female-flat-seat-45-elbow) is the alternative, so check the seat and the angle on the equipment before ordering the BSP swivel female flat seat (90° elbow).

faqs.q: What is the Male BSPT tapered used for?
faqs.a: The Male BSPT tapered is a 316L stainless-steel straight hose fitting with a tapered R thread from R1/8 to R2 that seals on the thread itself as it is tightened. It screws into a female BSP port that takes a tapered or parallel Rp thread, and is used on stainless hose assemblies where the thread joint, not a washer or cone, is the seal.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Male BSPT tapered come in?
faqs.a: The Male BSPT tapered is listed from R1/8 to R2 in taper thread. The listing gives the range, not a part-number table, so send the thread size and hose bore for us to confirm the exact part.

faqs.q: Can a Male BSPT tapered fitting go into a BSPP port?
faqs.a: A tapered R thread engages a parallel BSPP thread poorly and may leak or damage the port, so match taper to taper (or to a parallel Rp port that is designed for it). For a parallel male thread use the [BSP Male Flat Seat](/p/bsp-male-flat-seat) or the 60° cone version.

faqs.q: What pressure rating does the Male BSPT tapered have?
faqs.a: The listing gives the Male BSPT tapered no pressure figure of its own: the pressure of the finished assembly tracks the hose grade and ferrule when it is crimped to the correct diameter. Pick the hose first, then confirm that the hose rating suits the BSPT R1/8 to R2 port before you order.

faqs.q: What is the Male BSPT tapered made from, and where does stainless suit it?
faqs.a: The Male BSPT tapered is machined from 316L stainless steel, passivated with no plating, so its corrosion resistance comes from the native oxide layer. It suits marine, chemical, food-grade and washdown service where zinc-plated carbon steel corrodes. The listing gives -40°C to +200°C, limited by the hose and any O-ring.

faqs.q: Which standards does the Male BSPT tapered follow?
faqs.a: The Male BSPT tapered is listed to ISO 7-1, the standard for pipe threads where the joint is made on the thread, with ISO 228-1 also named for the parallel BSPP fittings in the family. The external thread is a taper R thread.

faqs.q: What does the Male BSPT tapered connect to?
faqs.a: It screws into a female taper (Rc) or parallel (Rp) BSP port as defined in ISO 7-1. The hose side takes an SS316L crimp ferrule; see our [stainless crimp hose fittings](/c/stainless-crimp-hose-fittings) for the stainless hose ends.

faqs.q: How should a stainless BSPT tapered thread be sealed?
faqs.a: Use a PTFE tape or an anti-seize sealant suitable for stainless steel on the taper thread and tighten by turns, not to a torque: the thread seals as it wedges. Stainless taper threads gall readily, so never over-tighten, and avoid reusing a fitting that has been run hard.

faqs.q: Where is a stainless male BSPT thread used on hose assemblies?
faqs.a: It is used on stainless hose assemblies that screw into BSPT or Rp ports on pumps, valves and instrument connections in marine, chemical and washdown plant. The [why fittings seize in coastal air](/blog/why-fittings-seize-in-coastal-air) article covers galling and corrosion risks.

faqs.q: Male BSPT tapered or BSP male-parallel 60° cone: how do they differ?
faqs.a: The Male BSPT tapered has an R taper thread that seals on the thread, while the [BSP male-parallel 60° cone](/p/bsp-male-parallel-60-cone) has a parallel thread and seals on a 60° cone. They fit different ports, so identify the port thread first.
